instructions: Rinse the 1 1/2 cups jasmine rice and get it cooking before anything else.
Pat the 1.25 lb pork dry and slice it as thinly as you can, about 1/8 inch thick.

Mince 6 of the garlic cloves. Put the pork in a bowl with the minced garlic, 1 tsp white pepper and the 1/2 tsp salt and work it together with your hands for about a minute. Leave it for 10 minutes while you do the rest.

Finely chop the other 8 garlic cloves. Put them in a wok or large skillet with the 1/4 cup oil over medium heat and stir all the time for 2 to 3 minutes, until the garlic is pale gold. Pull it off the heat as soon as it gets there. It keeps darkening in the hot oil and turns bitter if it goes brown.
Pour it through a metal strainer set over a heatproof bowl, so you keep the oil. Spread the crispy garlic out on a paper towel.
Stir the 2 tbsp oyster sauce and the 1 tbsp + 1 tsp soy sauce together in a small bowl. Slice the cucumber into rounds and roughly chop a handful of the cilantro.

Wipe out the wok and heat half the garlic oil in it over high until it shimmers. Add half the pork, spread it out and leave it for about a minute, until the underside is browned. Stir fry for another minute, until there's no pink left on the outside, and transfer it onto a plate.
Add the rest of the garlic oil and cook the other half of the pork the same way.
Put all the pork back in the wok, pour in the oyster sauce mixture and stir for about a minute.
Sprinkle the 1 tbsp sugar over the pork and stir fry for 1 to 2 minutes, until the sauce turns thick and sticky and the pork is a glossy dark brown.
Add 2 tbsp water and scrape up the browned bits from the bottom of the wok. Cook for about a minute more, until it's sticky again. Cut into a thick slice. It's done when there's no pink left.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a splash more soy sauce.
Serve over the jasmine rice with the last 1/4 tsp white pepper, the crispy garlic and the cilantro scattered on top, and the cucumber slices on the side.
method_notes: All three cook thin pork with a lot of garlic and a salty, slightly sweet sauce and serve it over jasmine rice. Thai Cookbook TV fries a batch of chopped garlic until crisp for the top, stir fries the pork with a little fresh garlic, adds oyster sauce and light soy, then sugar until it goes dry and sticky, deglazes with a spoonful of water and finishes with a dash of white pepper and cilantro. Cooking with Nart pounds white peppercorns with garlic and rubs it into salted pork before frying, with sweet soy for color and cucumber on the side, and Hungry in Thailand fries garlic, coriander root and black pepper before adding the pork and oyster, light and dark soy. This one follows the lead's sauce and crispy garlic with the pepper and garlic rubbed into the pork first, and cooks the stir fry in the garlic oil.
